messages:
maria.g: Kicking off staged canary shift for v2.3.0 in eu-west — moving from 5% -> 15%. Change window open until 21:00. Will call stop/go in 10m if anything looks off.

deploy-bot: [deploy] triggered by maria.g — canary_id=can-20240304-01; target=15%; status=warming; watch: latency_tail, 5xx_rate, embed-quality; automated alerts to eng-releases + oncall. Logs: /deploy/logs/can-20240304-01

sam: Quick check: no new 5xx spikes, tail latency +5% but within our threshold. Dashboard: https://internal/obs/can-20240304-01 (look at p99 and percentage above baseline).

kevin: saw one short latency spike at 15:12 in eu-west-1 — correlates with a routing refresh earlier. Infra said it was a harmless reconnect. Metrics came back down within 2m.

olivia: Can we hold before any further ramp to 30%? Want a QA pass on long-context formatting prompts. ping @maria.g :hand:

maria.g: Hold. Pausing any further ramp. Pinning v2.3.0 at 15% until QA signoff. Trigger condition: rollback if 5xx_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m OR latency_tail > 20% for 5m. Otherwise keep paused.

deploy-bot: Action: autoscale paused for can-20240304-01 (autoscale=false). Fallback version set to v2.2.9. To resume run: `/deploy resume can-20240304-01`

sam: Running a focused eval on the new prompt set now. Noticed a tiny format flip on math outputs for 3/50 samples — logging in RL-512. Assigning to @kevin to triage.

kevin: On it. Likely float formatting change due to tokenizer preproc tweak. If it's widespread we'll rollback. ETA ~20m to root cause.

olivia: Plan: if QA thumbs up before 20:40 we give green to resume. If not, we'll escalate for stop/go at 20:45. :thumbsup::hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled stop/go at 1712351100 — deploybot will post summary and pause/resume commands. Join ops call if we need to decide.

maria.g: Good call. I'll draft this into the release notes: "Canary paused at 15% pending QA for formatting issue; no customer-facing errors observed; rollback threshold set." Updating RL-512 and the changelog draft now.
